state: JevCode site iteration planning, round 3. Prior Jev rounds concluded: iteration focus = experience (0.94); infra-heavy iteration (3.0/4); playground should use bundled mocked samples (1.0 confidence, no serverless proxy); search valued 0.65; trust pass 0.54; comparison articles 0.33. The site is a static Astro 7 site, 8 languages (zh en ja ko de fr es pt), 39 docs in zh/en, 20 in others with en fallback, plus ecosystem page and case studies. Decided direction: build an interactive 'judgment playground' page where visitors experience Jev's evaluation model hands-on using pre-recorded real API responses. Now designing the playground page itself. Design questions: (1) How many demo scenarios should it have? Options: 3, 5, or 8. (2) Should scenarios be tied to the site's existing case-study pages (e.g. autoformat, rerank, guardrails) so the playground doubles as an index? (3) What UI elements best show 'judgment vs generation'? Options: probability bars per option, animated confidence gauge, side-by-side 'generative rewrite' vs 'judgment answer', or before/after text diff. (4) Should visitors be able to edit the input text of a scenario, with the response staying mocked (clearly labeled as cached/sample), or keep inputs fixed for honesty? (5) Where should the playground live in the site nav? Options: top nav item on all languages, linked only from the case-studies section, or as the hero CTA on the homepage.

scenario_count.instructions: How many demo scenarios should the playground ship with?

criteria.three: 3 scenarios: one per primitive (noul, choice, score) — minimal, focused
criteria.five: 5 scenarios: 3 primitives plus 2 pipeline cases (composite, fan-out)
criteria.eight: 8 scenarios: mirror the case-study taxonomy fully

tie_to_case_studies.instructions: Should scenarios link to their corresponding case-study doc pages so the playground doubles as an entry index?

criteria.true: Yes: each scenario ends with 'read the full cookbook' links

best_ui_element.instructions: Which UI element best communicates 'judgment, not generation' to a first-time visitor?

criteria.prob_bars: Probability bars per option with numeric values
criteria.gen_vs_judge: Side-by-side: what a generative model would output vs Jev's typed judgment

editable_inputs.instructions: Should visitors be able to edit scenario inputs while responses stay clearly-labeled cached samples?

criteria.true: Yes, editable inputs with honest 'cached sample' labeling; encourages play
criteria.false: No, fixed inputs; avoids confusion when the answer does not match the edited input

nav_placement.instructions: Where should the playground live in site navigation?

criteria.top_nav: Top nav item on all languages: maximum discoverability
criteria.cases_section: Linked from the case-studies section only: contextual
criteria.hero_cta: Homepage hero CTA: 'try it' as the first thing visitors see

honesty_labeling_critical.instructions: Is it critical that mocked responses be explicitly labeled as pre-recorded samples (not live inference)?

criteria.true: Yes: unlabeled mocks would mislead developers and damage trust
